question_text: Construct recommend(items, target, score) in Python. items is nonempty; score(item, target) returns an integer suitability. Return the item with highest suitability, breaking equal-suitability ties by greater item.stock. If both are equal, keep the first item. Negative suitability is possible.
adaptation_rationale: Corrects official sample lexicographic bug; retains object-list selection with primary/secondary/first-tie policy and tests counter examples.

marking_points.criterion: Initializes best and best score from an actual first item.
Visits remaining items and computes suitability.
Replaces best whenever suitability is strictly higher, regardless of stock.
On equal suitability, replaces only if stock is greater.
Keeps first when both metrics tie and updates cached score with best.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent technically correct wording or valid implementation earning the specified independent points.
partial_credit_notes: Award each stated point independently up to the total; do not double-credit the same idea.

verification.technical: Concrete marking points independently reasoned from the defined context and exact 2027 scope.
verification.code_check: Executable checks saved under checks/ where applicable.

test_code:
from types import SimpleNamespace
a=SimpleNamespace(score=-2,stock=100);b=SimpleNamespace(score=3,stock=1);c=SimpleNamespace(score=3,stock=2);d=SimpleNamespace(score=3,stock=2)
f=lambda item,target:item.score
assert recommend([a,b,c,d],None,f) is c
assert recommend([a,b],None,f) is b
assert recommend([a],None,f) is a
